questions.question: Which parameter was changed to see how well the battery pack could cool itself?

explanations.a: Cell voltage was not used to evaluate the cooling performance of the battery pack.
explanations.b: Cooling efficiency was varied to study how effectively heat could be removed from the battery pack.
explanations.c: Isolation response time is an output parameter observed during the simulation.
explanations.d: Fault duration determines when the fault occurs, not the cooling capability.

questions.question: What did you observe when the battery temperature was increased?

explanations.a: Higher temperatures do not reduce thermal propagation.
explanations.b: Temperature changes directly affect battery behavior.
explanations.c: Increasing the battery temperature caused heat to spread more quickly to nearby cells.
explanations.d: The simulation does not automatically remove faults.

questions.question: Which output value tells you how fast the isolation system reacted to the fault?

explanations.a: This shows the overall temperature of the battery pack.
explanations.b: Isolation response time indicates how quickly the protection system responded.
explanations.c: Cooling efficiency is an input parameter.
explanations.d: Fault duration is controlled by the user.

questions.question: What happened to the affected cells when the cooling efficiency was reduced?

answers.a: The number of affected cells decreased
answers.b: The number of affected cells remained unchanged
answers.c: The number of affected cells increased

explanations.a: Lower cooling efficiency does not reduce cell damage.
explanations.b: The extent of thermal propagation changes with cooling efficiency.
explanations.c: Reduced cooling efficiency allowed heat to spread to more cells.
explanations.d: Thermal runaway still affects neighboring cells.

questions.question: When did the battery isolation system become active during the simulation?

answers.b: When the safety temperature limit was reached
answers.d: When the battery pack cooled down

explanations.a: The isolation system activates only when a critical condition occurs.
explanations.b: The system was triggered after the faulty cell exceeded the safety threshold.
explanations.c: Cooling efficiency does not directly activate isolation.

questions.question: What was the effect of increasing the fault duration?

answers.c: More cells were affected by the fault

explanations.a: Longer faults generally increase battery damage.
explanations.c: A longer fault duration allowed heat to spread to additional cells.
explanations.d: The simulation does not remove faults automatically.

questions.question: Which output helped you identify the extent of thermal runaway in the battery pack?

explanations.a: Fault trigger time only indicates when the fault started.
explanations.b: Cooling efficiency is an input parameter.
explanations.c: The number of affected cells shows how far the thermal runaway spread.
explanations.d: Cell voltage does not directly indicate propagation extent.

questions.question: What happened after the faulty battery section was disconnected from the rest of the pack?

explanations.a: Isolation is intended to limit damage, not increase it.
explanations.b: Disconnecting the faulty section reduced the spread of heat to nearby cells.
explanations.c: The cooling system continues to function normally.
explanations.d: Isolation does not affect fault duration.

questions.question: Under which conditions was thermal runaway observed to be the most severe?

answers.a: Low temperature and high cooling efficiency
answers.b: High temperature and high cooling efficiency
answers.c: High temperature and low cooling efficiency
answers.d: Low temperature and short fault duration

explanations.a: These conditions help reduce thermal propagation.
explanations.c: High temperature combined with poor cooling resulted in the most severe thermal runaway.
explanations.d: These conditions reduce the severity of the fault.

questions.question: Which factor was most effective in preventing further battery damage during the simulation?

explanations.b: Delayed response allows heat to spread further.
explanations.c: A faster isolation response limited thermal propagation and protected nearby cells.
